modules.name: True-north and solar frame
modules.design_question: Where is true north in the model, and where is the sun, in Vancouver clock time (PDT or PST per rule), for every study date the other modules need?
modules.effort: S: about 3-4 dev-days (calendar presets and per-rule time zones added in r1)
inputs: Layer 0 model coordinate frame (which axis is Y, units)
Site latitude/longitude (default about 49.283 N, 123.12 W; user-editable)
North reference: site-plan north-arrow angle, Rhino North setting, Revit True North or IFC TrueNorth, if present
Study calendar: dates, clock times and a time-zone tag per rule (tz database America/Vancouver; PDT on 22 Sept, PST on 11 Nov)

parameters.name: North angle (model +Y to true north)
parameters.relationship: All shadow, sun-hour and facade results rotate by this angle; a 45-degree error moves a shadow from one downtown street axis to the other. Rhino North is CCW from +X (default 90 deg); Ladybug north_angle is CCW from +Y.

parameters.name: Street-grid rotation vs true north
parameters.relationship: Downtown grid is rotated about 45 degrees (Granville about 045, West Georgia about 315, from OSM geometry), so street-aligned facades face NE/SE/SW/NW; orientation classes must use true north, not model axes.

parameters.name: Clock time and zone (PDT/PST)
parameters.relationship: Policy hours are Pacific clock hours: 22 Sept is PDT (UTC-7), 11 Nov is PST (UTC-8). Solar noon is 13:05 PDT on 22 Sept and 11:56 PST on 11 Nov (NOAA recomputation); a PST/PDT mix-up shifts the sun 15 degrees.

parameters.name: Latitude
parameters.relationship: At 49.28 N the noon sun is 40.8 degrees high at the equinox and 17.3 degrees at the winter solstice (NOAA recomputation), so shadow length per metre of height is about 1.16 and 3.21; at 10:00 PST on 11 Nov it is 3.0.

parameters.name: Solar-position algorithm
parameters.relationship: Shadow-edge error equals error angle times shadow length; SunCalc 2.x states about 0.08 degrees (under 1 m on a 600 m shadow, derived), with degrees clockwise from north and refraction-corrected altitude. pvlib spa_python gives NREL SPA with apparent_elevation.

metrics.name: Model-north agreement between explicit references
metrics.good: Explicit references (site-plan arrow, IFC TrueNorth, Rhino North, Revit True North) agree within 1 degree; OSM-implied grid bearing within about 3 degrees
metrics.bad: Explicit references disagree by more than 1 degree, or none exists: block downstream modules and ask the user. OSM disagreement above about 3 degrees: warning only
metrics.basis: Editable tolerances for drawing precision. OSM bearing is only an estimate for a hypothetical site, so it warns but never blocks (r1 change).
metrics.method: Compare north arrow, IFC TrueNorth / Rhino North, and OSM street-bearing-implied angle.

metrics.name: Assuming model +Y is true north
metrics.good: North angle read from the site-plan arrow; expect roughly 45 degrees offset for a street-aligned model
metrics.bad: Treating drawing-up as north on this site
metrics.basis: City states the downtown grid is rotated; OSM bearings of Granville (about 44.7 deg) and West Georgia (about 314.8 deg) computed for this packet and reproduced by the round-1 reviewer. The VTC brief also says the north arrow is rotated.

metrics.name: Time-zone offset per study date
metrics.good: 22 Sept = UTC-7 (PDT); 11 Nov = UTC-8 (PST); offsets come from the tz database per rule
metrics.bad: One fixed offset for all rules, or PST on 22 Sept
metrics.basis: v1 said all policy hours are PDT. The cenotaph rule (s.4.3.1, reviewer reading) is in PST on 11 Nov. DST ended Sunday 1 Nov 2026 (calendar computed), so 11 Nov is PST.
metrics.method: Unit-test offsets with tzdata for 22 Sept and 11 Nov 2026.

metrics.name: Sun-position error
metrics.good: At most 0.1 degree (SunCalc 2.x README states about 0.08)
metrics.bad: Above 0.5 degree (unvalidated implementation)
metrics.basis: Good value from the SunCalc README (opened); bad value is an editable preset.
metrics.method: Unit-test pinned suncalc >= 2.0 against pvlib spa_python (apparent elevation vs apparent altitude, and azimuth) for Vancouver at 10:00, 13:05, 16:00 PDT on 22 Sept (fixtures: 26.9 deg / 125.9 deg at 10:00; 28.1 / 231.6 at 16:00) and 09:00 PST on 21 Dec (low sun, refraction matters).

modules.method: 1) Take north from the highest-confidence source: explicit site-plan arrow, then IFC TrueNorth, then Rhino or Revit setting; store as angle CCW from +Y. 2) Convert conventions: Ladybug north_angle = Rhino North angle (CCW from +X) minus 90. 3) Build the study calendar with the tz database (America/Vancouver), never fixed offsets; tag each rule PDT or PST. 4) Compute apparent altitude and azimuth (clockwise from true north) with pvlib spa_python or SunCalc 2.x, then rotate sun vectors into the model frame. 5) Block downstream modules only if explicit references disagree by more than 1 degree; warn if the OSM street bearing differs by more than about 3 degrees. 6) Emit NorthFrame and SunVectorSet.
visualization: Stereographic sun-path diagram with equinox and solstice arcs; the 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 PDT window and the 11 Nov 10:00-12:00 PST window highlighted in two colours
Plan view with two arrows (model Y and true north) plus street-grid bearing; red banner when explicit references disagree, amber when only OSM disagrees
Brief's named directions (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet/North Shore) drawn on the rotated site plan as a visual cross-check
outputs: SunVectorSet [{rule_id, local_time, tz, utc_offset_h, azimuth_true_deg, apparent_altitude_deg, vector_model_frame}]

StudyCalendar presets: BasicStudy 22 Sept 10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00 PDT; DetailedStudy 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 every 15 min (25 instants) PDT; RemembranceDay 11 Nov 10:00-12:00 PST (15-min default); optional extra dates 20 Mar, 21 Jun, 21 Dec (design exploration; further dates may be required by s.3.1.4)
modules.human_judgment: Confirm which north the site plan uses and its sign; choose study dates beyond the policy dates; prefer a surveyed grid angle over the OSM estimate.
modules.limits: North stays an input unless the file stores it. The OSM-derived grid bearing (about 45 degrees) is an estimate, not a survey, and cannot be tied to one street on a hypothetical site. Magnetic declination is not applied; never use magnetic north. Solar algorithms ignore terrain, atmosphere and shading. Results depend on the clock-time convention the user selects.

libraries.name: SunCalc (JS), pinned at 2.0 or later
libraries.role: in-browser sun position (degrees clockwise from north, refraction-corrected altitude)

modules.name: Vancouver downtown solar-access (new-shadow) test
modules.design_question: Does the proposal cast new shadow on protected public spaces under the Downtown Peninsula guidelines, per rule and time, and where must the massing be cut?
modules.effort: L: about 10-14 dev-days, including the Table-1 data file, terrain-aware shadow casting and the Basic and Detailed study outputs
inputs: SunVectorSet and NorthFrame from P02-M01 (rule-specific instants and time zones)
Proposed massing (Layer 0 geometry)
Context scenarios: existing plus approved built context; plus known proposed developments (user import)
Terrain mesh from City DEM, LiDAR or contours (Open Government Licence - Vancouver) covering the site and every protected space
Versioned Table-1 protected-space GeoJSON: polygon, class, clause, hours, time zone, exception flags (parks seeded from City open data, plazas digitised)
Study preset: BasicStudy, DetailedStudy, RemembranceDay, or hourly exploration

parameters.name: Protected-space class (Table 1)
parameters.relationship: Class selects clause and result type: parks, schools and s.4.2 plazas get a 0 m2 test (3.1.1); other plazas and West End miniparks only minimise (3.2.1); Villages use the north sidewalk (3.3.1). Misclassifying a space flips pass/fail.

parameters.name: Study window and time zone per rule
parameters.relationship: Parks and schools 10:00-16:00 PT on 22 Sept; Davie Village 10:00-16:00, Robson Village 10:00-15:00; cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 PST on 11 Nov. Longer windows cut more massing; the 11 Nov sun is lowest, so shadows are longest.

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: Shadow length is H / tan(sun altitude). On 22 Sept the sun is 26.9 degrees high at 10:00 and 28.1 at 16:00 PDT, so 300 m of height throws about 592 m and 561 m; at 10:00 PST on 11 Nov (18.3 degrees), about 905 m.

parameters.name: Shadow bearing
parameters.relationship: On 22 Sept the shadow bearing sweeps 306 (10:00), 339 (12:00), 18 (14:00) to 52 degrees (16:00), roughly along the two downtown street axes; on 11 Nov it runs 331 to 1 degrees. Spaces NW, N and NE of the tower are at risk.

parameters.name: Level difference to the protected space
parameters.relationship: A receiver lying dz below the site adds about dz x 1.9-2.0 m of shadow reach at 10:00 and 16:00 on 22 Sept; 20 m of fall moves a shadow edge about 40 m, enough to flip pass/fail (derived).

parameters.name: Floor-plate width perpendicular to the sun
parameters.relationship: Wider plate gives a wider shadow band and longer dwell time on any point (geometry). The City ties larger tower floor plates to solar-access compliance, but those figures were not opened.

parameters.name: Exception requested
parameters.relationship: A fail becomes a case-by-case exception only for social housing, below-market rental, a public childcare facility, heritage conservation or a major city-building priority (3.1.2), with a shadow rationale statement and Detailed study (5.2). Council removed the blanket social-housing exemption.

parameters.name: Time step and study type
parameters.relationship: Basic study uses 4 instants (10, 12, 14, 16 PT); Detailed uses 25 at 15 min, about 3.6 times the compute of hourly. A 2-hour step can miss a short incursion by a narrow tower shadow (derived).

parameters.name: Baseline scenario choice
parameters.relationship: New shadow is measured against existing plus approved context with topography; adding known proposed developments to the baseline lowers the new shadow attributed to the proposal where shadows overlap, so the scenario must be stated (5.1).

metrics.name: New shadow on parks, schools and s.4.2 plazas (inside property lines)
metrics.good: 0 m2 at every instant, 10:00-16:00 PT on 22 Sept (3.1.1, 4.2.1)
metrics.bad: Above 0 m2 at any instant: guideline not met; exception case (3.1.2) or cut the massing
metrics.basis: Clause text read by the round-1 reviewer in the PDF (approved 17 Sept 2025, amended 29 July 2026); packet author's fetch was blocked. Corroborated by opened press and UDI summaries. Area tolerance unknown.
metrics.method: Polygon difference of proposal shadow minus baseline shadow, clipped to each property-line polygon, per instant.

metrics.name: Other urban plazas and West End miniparks (not upgraded by s.4.2)
metrics.good: No pass/fail: report new-shadow m2 and coverage % and show that reductions were tried 'where possible' (3.2.1)
metrics.bad: A 0 m2 pass/fail applied to them, or no report
metrics.basis: v1 applied the zero-shadow test to all plazas and miniparks; the reviewer's reading of 3.2.1 says only minimise where possible.

metrics.name: Plazas moved up to the park rule: Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square, Dilawri Square South
metrics.good: 0 m2 at every instant, 10:00-16:00 PT on 22 Sept (3.1 via 4.2.1); exceptions possible under 3.1.2
metrics.bad: Any new shadow with no exception case
metrics.basis: Replaces v1 'Library Square south plaza: absolute no new shadow', taken from draft coverage (S06). Reviewer: only Sun Yat-Sen has no exception clause.

metrics.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Garden/Park
metrics.good: No new shadow at any instant, 10:00-16:00 PT on 22 Sept (4.1.1); the only rule with no exception clause
metrics.bad: Any new shadow
metrics.basis: Draft coverage (S06) and the reviewer's reading of the approved text agree.

metrics.name: Village north sidewalks: Davie 10:00-16:00, Robson 10:00-15:00
metrics.unit: m2 per instant (curb to building face)
metrics.good: 0 m2 at every instant in each window, 22 Sept (3.3.1(a)-(b))
metrics.bad: Above 0 m2 at any instant in the window
metrics.basis: Draft coverage gives Davie 10-16 and Robson 10-15 (S06); UDI says north sidewalk of Davie Village (S07); the reviewer read 3.3.1.

metrics.name: Victory Square cenotaph circle
metrics.good: No shadow on the circle 10:00-12:00 PST on 11 Nov (4.3.1); exceptions only after comprehensive public and stakeholder engagement (4.3.2)
metrics.bad: Any shadow on the circle in that window
metrics.basis: v1 said 11:00 on Remembrance Day (draft coverage, S05, S06). Approved text per reviewer: 10:00-12:00 PST. Victory Square is outside the CDDG area (S09) but inside this guideline.

metrics.name: Assessment dates and window
metrics.good: 22 Sept only (plus 11 Nov for the cenotaph), per-rule windows; spring equinox optional extra; further dates may be required (3.1.4)
metrics.bad: Spring-equinox (20/21 Mar) test treated as required downtown, or 22 Sept run in PST
metrics.basis: Downtown guidelines eliminated the spring-equinox consideration; the older approach ran spring to fall equinox.

metrics.name: Basic study completeness
metrics.good: 4 instants (10, 12, 14, 16 PT), geolocated, UTC-7, complete context with terrain, new shadow visually delineated from existing (5.1)
metrics.bad: Missing instants, wrong time zone, flat ground or incomplete context
metrics.basis: Reviewer read ss.5.1-5.2 in the PDF; v1 search excerpts (2-hour intervals, 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 PDT) agree.

metrics.name: Detailed study outputs and Shadow Coverage %
metrics.good: 25 instants (15 min, 10:00-16:00 inclusive) with m2 take-offs of existing, proposed-additional and cumulative shadow; coverage % = sum of interval areas / (space area x 25) (5.2(b)-(c))
metrics.bad: An exception sought without a Detailed study
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Formula and 25-instant count quoted only by the round-1 reviewer; no numeric coverage limit was reported, so none is applied.

metrics.name: Baseline and context completeness
metrics.good: Complete built and approved context with topography out to about 1 km (11 Nov shadow reach for 300 m is about 905 m), plus known proposed developments as a separate scenario; trees and shade structures excluded (5.1, 5.1.1)
metrics.bad: Flat ground plane, partial context, or trees counted in the baseline
metrics.basis: v1 projected prisms onto a flat ground plane against an existing-plus-approved baseline only.

modules.method: 1) Load the versioned Table-1 dataset (class, clause, hours, time zone per space) and keep spaces inside the shadow reach of the massing. 2) Build three scenarios on a terrain mesh: existing plus approved; plus known proposed; plus proposal. Leave trees, shade structures and small park outbuildings out of the baseline. 3) Take each rule instants from P02-M01: Basic 4, Detailed 25, 11 Nov 10:00-12:00 PST. 4) Cast shadows onto terrain and onto each space at its real elevation. 5) New shadow = proposal minus baseline, clipped to property lines (parks, plazas) or the north sidewalk (Villages). 6) Parks, schools, s.4.2 plazas, Sun Yat-Sen and Villages pass only at 0 m2 at every instant; other plazas and miniparks get m2 and coverage percent, no pass/fail. 7) Detailed study: coverage percent = sum of interval areas / (space area x 25). 8) Store the clause reference with every result.
visualization: Plan view on terrain: baseline shadow in grey, new shadow in red hatch, protected polygons outlined by class colour; hour slider with Basic ticks (10, 12, 14, 16) and 15-min Detailed ticks
Per-space result card: PASS/FAIL badge for 0 m2 classes, 'MINIMISE - report' badge for plazas and miniparks, each linked to its clause number
Table of m2 of new shadow by space and instant; bar of Shadow Coverage % for existing, proposed-additional and cumulative series
3D elevation-aware view showing receiver levels versus site level
Optional translucent solar-envelope volume over the site showing maximum compliant height
outputs: PolicyResult[] {space_id, class, clause_ref, instant_local, tz, new_shadow_m2, result_type (pass_fail | minimise_report), pass, coverage_pct}
BasicStudy sheet (4 instants, new shadow delineated) and DetailedStudy tables (25 instants; existing, proposed-additional, cumulative m2; coverage %)
ShadowMask per instant and scenario (existing+approved, +known proposed, +proposal) as Mesh3D or Polygon2D
ExceptionFlags and a Shadow Rationale Statement stub with the 3.1.2 grounds and 3.1.3 staff considerations (topography, duration, vulnerable users) as structured fields
modules.human_judgment: Whether to meet the rule, seek an exception, or breach it deliberately and argue public benefit (the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded); correct classification of each space; which known proposed developments count; trade-off against height and the 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum.
modules.limits: Clauses come from the round-1 reviewer reading of the July 2026 PDF, which the packet author could not open: a second reader must confirm Table 1 before any board claim, and again after the CDDG takes effect on 27 Oct 2026. The VTC site is hypothetical. Shadow only: no sky-diffuse light or glare. Context must reach about 1 km. The City tolerance for new shadow is unknown.

modules.name: Public-realm sun-hours map
modules.design_question: How many hours of direct sun reach the plaza, sidewalks, mid-block connections and transit plaza on key dates, and which massing moves recover sun?
inputs: SunVectorSet and NorthFrame from P02-M01
Proposed massing and context massing on the terrain mesh
Public-realm polygons from Layer 0 tags (public, retail frontage, transit plaza, mid-block links)
Grid spacing, sensor offset and time step settings

parameters.name: Study date
parameters.relationship: Winter noon shadows are about 3.2 times height (21 Dec, NOAA recomputation), reaching far beyond the block, so December sun on plazas is set largely by neighbouring towers; summer noon shadows (about 0.5 times height) stay local.

parameters.name: Position of tall mass relative to public space
parameters.relationship: Midday shadows fall north: a tower north of a plaza leaves it sunlit, one south of it shades it. East vs west only trades morning for afternoon sun (symmetric about 13:05 PDT on 22 Sept); choose by use (geometry).

parameters.name: Podium height and setback
parameters.relationship: Higher street wall puts a wider shadow band over the sidewalk and ground-floor retail; a stepped podium on the sunny side reduces it (geometry). Plaza and sidewalk edges face NE/SE/SW/NW on this grid.

parameters.name: Sensor grid spacing
parameters.relationship: Finer spacing resolves shadow edges; cost grows with the inverse square of spacing (derived). Default 1 m is a team preset.

parameters.name: Sensor offset above ground
parameters.relationship: Offset 0 (the DirectSunStudy default) risks self-intersection with the ground mesh; use 0.05-0.1 m (team preset). SVF in P02-M08 uses 1.5 m because it describes the pedestrian view of the sky.

parameters.name: Time step
parameters.relationship: Sun hours equal sunlit samples divided by steps per hour, so a point's error is up to one time step; use 4 steps per hour for final figures (team preset).

parameters.name: Context radius
parameters.relationship: Shadow reach is about 2 times height at 10:00 and 16:00 on 22 Sept and 3.2 times at winter noon (derived); a 300 m tower needs about 1 km of context to capture winter shadows.

metrics.name: Share of each public open space with at least 2 h direct sun on 21 March (whole day), UK comparison
metrics.good: At least 50% of the area receives at least 2 h
metrics.bad: Less than 50% of the area receives 2 h
metrics.basis: BRE BR 209 amenity-area criterion recalled, not opened; written for UK housing amenity space, not a Vancouver requirement. r1: computed over sunrise-sunset on 21 March, not 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept.
metrics.method: Sum of sunlit time steps per sensor on 21 March, then area-weighted share of sensors with at least 2 h.

metrics.name: Change in sun hours vs baseline (existing plus approved context), design exploration on four dates
metrics.good: Zero or positive at every public-realm sensor
metrics.bad: Negative at any sensor: report the area-weighted loss
metrics.basis: v1 called this a verified City criterion. The City test covers only Table-1 spaces on 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 PT and plazas only minimise (see P02-M02). Now an editable team preset; policy badges appear only in P02-M02.
metrics.method: Delta grid = proposal minus baseline sun hours per date; descriptive, separate from the policy test.

modules.method: 1) Build a sensor mesh on the public-realm ground plane (default 1 m grid, offset 0.05-0.1 m) on the terrain mesh. 2) For each study date (22 Sept 10:00-16:00 PDT, 21 Mar, 21 Jun, 21 Dec) generate sun vectors at 4 steps per hour from P02-M01. 3) Cast each reversed sun vector from every sensor through proposal plus context (DirectSunStudy logic: sun hours = row sum of the intersection matrix divided by steps per hour). 4) Repeat with the baseline only. 5) Report sun hours per sensor, area share at or above the preset hours (2 h on 21 Mar, whole day, UK comparison) and delta vs baseline. 6) Colour the mesh with the Ecotect set over a 0-12 h legend. Use a three.js shadow-map layer for live preview only, never for reported numbers.
visualization: False-colour mesh on the ground plane, 0-12 h legend with 2 h contour lines
Small multiples for the four dates
Delta map: blue = sun gained, red = sun lost vs baseline (labelled 'design exploration, not the City test')
Bar chart: percent of each space with at least 2 h on 21 Mar, with the source and 'UK, unverified' printed on the bar
Time-slider shadow animation (preview only)
outputs: Per-point sun/shade flags by hour (feeds wind/thermal-comfort and public-realm modules)
modules.human_judgment: Which spaces deserve sun (retail high-street sidewalk, transit plaza, cultural or ceremonial space) and how much; morning versus afternoon preference by programme (cafe terrace vs quiet shaded seating); Indigenous and 'City in Nature' planting and gathering needs.
modules.limits: Direct sun only; Vancouver winters are mostly overcast, so sun hours overstate winter conditions. Trees, canopies and temporary structures are ignored. Geometry is static. The 2-hour threshold is UK practice and unverified; the City test lives in P02-M02. No comfort model: wind and temperature are separate modules.

modules.name: Facade and roof solar radiation and PV potential
modules.design_question: How much solar radiation reaches each facade and roof surface once neighbours are included, and where does PV or shading pay off on a grid rotated 45 degrees?
inputs: Proposed massing with surface types (roof, wall) from Layer 0
Context massing on the terrain mesh
Weather file (CWEC 2020 or TMYx EPW) and NorthFrame from P02-M01
Optional: window-to-wall ratio, PV coverage and efficiency presets (Advanced mode)

parameters.name: Surface orientation and tilt (true azimuth)
parameters.relationship: PVGIS-ERA5 vertical walls, kWh/m2/yr: S 1,072; SW 1,045; SE 955; W 809; E 688; NW 459; NE 388; N 242 (peak 1,082 at 15 degrees west of south). Roof 1,245 flat, 1,514 at 40-degree tilt. A north-angle error moves faces between classes.

parameters.name: Context obstruction
parameters.relationship: More and closer obstructing towers cut direct and sky-diffuse radiation on lower floors; upper-tower and roof surfaces approach the unobstructed values (geometry).

parameters.name: Reflectance (ground and facades)
parameters.relationship: Higher albedo raises radiation on vertical surfaces (pvlib default 0.25). RadiationStudy has no inter-reflections except a ground hemisphere: conservative for PV yield, but non-conservative for overheating loads (P02-M05) where neighbours are glass.

parameters.name: Weather file
parameters.relationship: Annual totals scale with the file; CWEC 2020 and TMYx are available for Vancouver. Checking simulated unobstructed values against the PVGIS reference exposes file or north-angle errors.

parameters.name: PV efficiency and coverage ratio
parameters.relationship: Yield is incident radiation times efficiency times performance ratio times covered area. PVGIS 1 kWp yields at 14% loss, kWh/kWp/yr: roof 978; S wall 843; SW 823; SE 750; NW 329; NE 273.

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio
parameters.relationship: Radiation is computed on the whole envelope; PV-usable area is roughly (1 minus WWR) times face area times coverage, so higher WWR reduces BIPV area and raises solar gain (see P02-M05).

metrics.name: Solar access ratio per face
metrics.unit: % of unobstructed irradiation at the face's own azimuth
metrics.good: At least 80%
metrics.bad: Below 50%
metrics.basis: Editable preset. Reference is now a PVGIS azimuth curve (24 bins of 15 degrees, queried in r1), not four cardinal values; PVGIS values verified, cut-offs unsourced. Compagnon 2004 recalled, not opened.
metrics.method: Face irradiation from the radiation study divided by the PVGIS value for the face azimuth (tilt 90) or the roof (tilt 0), interpolated between bins.

metrics.name: PV specific yield on candidate faces
metrics.good: At least 700 (editable): unobstructed SW (823), SE (750) and roof (978) reach it; NW (329) and NE (273) never do
metrics.bad: Below 420 (half the south-wall reference of 843)
metrics.basis: v1 good cut-off of 843 equals a due-south wall, which a street-aligned tower on a 45-degree grid does not have, so no face could pass. Reference yields are verified PVGIS outputs; the cut-offs are team presets.

metrics.name: Simulated unobstructed irradiation vs PVGIS reference
metrics.good: Within plus or minus 10%
metrics.bad: Beyond plus or minus 20%: check weather file and north angle
metrics.basis: QA tolerance chosen by team; ERA5 bias was not assessed.

modules.method: 1) Sub-divide facade and roof faces into a sensor mesh. 2) Build a cumulative sky matrix from the EPW (Perez-type sky, Reinhart patches) and rotate it by the NorthFrame. 3) Run the radiation study: intersect sensor rays with context geometry on terrain to get visible sky and ground, add direct, diffuse and ground-reflected terms; output kWh/m2 and W/m2 (no inter-reflections). 4) Divide each face value by the PVGIS reference at the face own azimuth to get the solar access ratio. 5) Estimate PV yield with pvlib transposition (get_total_irradiance, Perez or Hay-Davies) and a performance ratio. 6) State the bias direction per downstream use: conservative for PV yield, non-conservative for overheating (see P02-M05). 7) Print thresholds and their status next to each result.
visualization: False-colour mesh on the massing, kWh/m2/yr legend with tick marks at the PVGIS unobstructed values for N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW walls and the roof
Azimuth curve chart: PVGIS reference line (15-degree bins) with each face plotted at its true azimuth
Radiation rose or dome for a selected surface; monthly bar chart per selected face
Per-face table with solar access ratio badge showing threshold status (team assumption)
outputs: Hourly irradiance on glazing (feeds P02-M05, energy and carbon, MEP and facade modules)
modules.human_judgment: Whether facade PV or BIPV suits the design and cultural intent (the jury penalises generic design); trade-offs with views, daylight and expression; acceptable payback.
modules.limits: No inter-reflections, so reflective glass neighbours are ignored: conservative for PV yield, non-conservative for overheating loads. Weather files are typical years, not extremes. PVGIS-ERA5 values are satellite-reanalysis and unvalidated here. Facade PV thresholds are team presets. Cost, tree shading, snow and soiling are not modelled.

modules.name: Solar gain and overheating screening
modules.design_question: Which facades and floors carry the highest warm-season solar load on glazing, how does shading change heating-season gain, and what does that mean for TEDI?
modules.effort: M: about 5-7 dev-days for screening; thermal model is a separate packet
inputs: Hourly irradiance on facades from P02-M04
Window-to-wall ratio by orientation and floor (Layer 0 or Advanced presets)
Glazing SHGC and VT presets (Advanced mode)
Program tags (office, residential, hotel) and weather file, including future-climate file
Optional multi-bounce irradiance for floors facing glazed neighbours

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio by orientation
parameters.relationship: Solar load on glazing scales with glazed area times irradiation times SHGC, so raising WWR on west-facing walls (SW, NW on this grid) raises peak load roughly in proportion (physics).

parameters.name: Facade orientation
parameters.relationship: West vertical receives about 17% more annual irradiation than east (809 vs 688 kWh/m2/yr); on this grid SW gets 1,045 vs NW 459 and SE 955 vs NE 388, so glazing orientation drives load.

parameters.name: Shading projection (overhang and fin angles)
parameters.relationship: Larger overhang or fin projection masks more of the sky dome seen by the glazing and lowers direct gain; Ladybug Sky Mask accepts overhang and fin projection angles for a chosen orientation.

parameters.name: Program and internal gains
parameters.relationship: Program sets internal gains and occupancy hours, so identical solar load has different overheating consequences for hotel, residential and office floors; values come from Advanced-mode presets, not sourced here.

parameters.name: Climate scenario
parameters.relationship: Typical-year files understate future warm-season hours; Canadian future-climate files are listed on Climate.OneBuilding (2022 set), allowing present vs future comparison.

parameters.name: Heating-season (Oct-Apr) useful gain
parameters.relationship: Winter glazing gain offsets heating demand and so lowers TEDI; shading that cuts June-September load also cuts October-April gain, so the best shading is orientation-specific (physics; TEDI target from HBP s.2.2).

parameters.name: Reflected gain from glazed neighbours
parameters.relationship: Reflections from glass neighbours raise glazing load on lower floors, which P02-M04 omits; an optional multi-bounce Radiance run (ambient bounces above 0) adds an allowance for floors facing glazed neighbours (physics).

metrics.name: Warm-season (Jun-Sep) irradiation on glazing by facade
metrics.good: At or below the building-wide mean
metrics.bad: More than 1.25 times the building-wide mean
metrics.basis: Relative ranking preset for screening; no sourced Vancouver threshold.

metrics.name: Thermal energy demand intensity (TEDI), needs a thermal model
metrics.good: At most 15 on the non-Passive-House route (HBP s.2.2), with TEUI/GHGI targets by use and a low-carbon energy connection
metrics.bad: Above 15 without Passive House certification
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Higher Buildings Policy (amended 31 Mar 2026) s.2.2 as read by the round-1 reviewer; by-use TEUI/GHGI values not transcribed; City Energy Modelling Guidelines returned HTTP 403.

metrics.name: Hours of exceedance of the adaptive comfort threshold (UK comparison, needs thermal model)
metrics.good: 3% or less
metrics.bad: More than 3%
metrics.basis: CIBSE TM52 (2013) exists, but its criteria were not displayed on the opened page; the 3% value is recalled. Vancouver's overheating limit (Passive House overheating frequency; City Energy Modelling Guidelines comfort limit) was not opened: the Passive House Institute page lists no numbers.

modules.method: 1) Take hourly irradiance on each facade face from P02-M04; for floors facing glazed neighbours optionally rerun with ambient bounces above 0. 2) Multiply by glazed fraction and SHGC (and a sky-mask shading factor when overhangs or fins are set) to get solar load on glazing in W/m2 of facade. 3) Aggregate to warm-season (Jun-Sep) kWh/m2 and peak hourly load per orientation and floor band, plus heating-season (Oct-Apr) useful gain. 4) Rank facades against the building mean. 5) Export loads to an EnergyPlus-class model to get TEDI against the HBP s.2.2 target and hours of exceedance against the adopted overheating criterion (to be confirmed). 6) Repeat with a future-climate file.
visualization: Unfolded facade elevation heat-map (W/m2) by orientation and floor band
Polar chart of warm-season load by azimuth, with heating-season gain as a second ring
Stereographic sky-mask diagram showing overhang or fin effect at a selected window
Present vs future-climate bar pair
outputs: ShadingEffectiveness (percent load reduction, and percent heating-season gain lost)
OverheatingRiskFlag per facade band (feeds energy, MEP cooling and facade/material modules)
modules.human_judgment: Acceptable overheating risk; passive vs mechanical cooling; facade expression versus shading; trade-off between summer shading, winter gain, daylight and views; Passive House versus TEDI route.
modules.limits: Screening only: no thermal mass, ventilation, blinds or occupant behaviour. The Passive House overheating criterion and the City Energy Modelling Guidelines comfort limit were not opened; TM52 is a UK comparison only. Weather and future files are scenarios, not forecasts. Glazing properties are presets until Advanced mode is filled. TEDI needs a thermal model outside this packet.

modules.name: Floor-plate depth-to-window daylight screen
modules.design_question: Which parts of each tower floor plate lie beyond practical daylight reach of the facade, by programme, before any simulation is run?
inputs: Floor-plate polygons per level and core footprint (Layer 0)
Facade lines with window-to-wall ratio and head height (Layer 0 or Advanced presets)
Programme tags per area (office, residential, hotel, core, mechanical)
Obstruction angle from context massing (optional)

parameters.name: Plate depth (window to core or far window)
parameters.relationship: Deeper plates leave a larger share of floor area beyond daylight reach (geometry); with a fixed core, widening the plate deepens the daylit band instead.

parameters.name: Window head height
parameters.relationship: Higher head height pushes daylight further in. Candidate sources: ASHRAE 90.1 sidelit zones (1 and 2 times head height) and the BRE/BS 8206-2 limiting-depth rule, both recalled, not opened; k = 2.0 stays a team assumption.

parameters.name: Glazing visual transmittance (VT)
parameters.relationship: VT below 0.4 can halve or more of the incoming light; VT above about 0.6 can cause glare, so VT trades daylight against glare.

parameters.name: Neighbour obstruction angle
parameters.relationship: A tall neighbour close to the facade raises the obstruction angle and lowers sky visible from lower-floor windows, shortening reach; upper floors recover (geometry).

parameters.name: Programme tag
parameters.relationship: Only regularly occupied programme (office, residential, hotel rooms) counts in the denominator; cores, mechanical and back-of-house are excluded, so the tagging in Layer 0 changes the result.

metrics.name: Share of regularly occupied area within daylight reach
metrics.good: At least 75%
metrics.bad: Below 40%
metrics.basis: Geometric proxy borrowing LEED sDA tiers (75% three credits, 55% two, 40% one) from the open-source LEED v4.1 implementation; reach factor k = 2.0 is unsourced.
metrics.method: Area of occupied polygon within k x head height of a window line divided by occupied area.

metrics.name: Average daylight factor of a typical room
metrics.good: Above 5% (well lit)
metrics.bad: Below 2% (artificial light needed throughout)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] CIBSE Lighting Guide 10 (1999) bands quoted via Wikipedia. Overcast-sky metric, not climate-based; UK practice is reported to have moved to EN 17037 illuminance targets (BR 209, 2022; not opened), so prefer P02-M07.
metrics.method: Split-flux style estimate from glazed area, VT, obstruction angle, surface reflectance and room area.

metrics.name: Limiting room depth (second check)
metrics.good: L/W + L/H at or below 2/(1 - Rb), with Rb the mean reflectance of the rear half of the room
metrics.bad: Above that limit: room too deep for sidelighting alone
metrics.basis: BRE / BS 8206-2 limiting-depth formula recalled, not opened; offered as an optional second check beside the team-assumption reach factor.

modules.method: 1) For each typical floor (lower, mid, upper) take occupied polygons by programme tag. 2) Build window lines from facade segments with WWR and head height. 3) Compute distance from each point (0.5 m grid) to the nearest window line; label facade orientation from the NorthFrame (street faces are NE/SE/SW/NW). 4) Daylight reach = k x head height (k = 2.0 preset; k = 1 and 2 mirror ASHRAE-style primary and secondary zones, to verify). 5) Share of occupied area within reach per programme. 6) Optional second check: limiting room depth L/W + L/H <= 2/(1 - Rb) (recalled). 7) Flag floors below the proxy thresholds and recommend running P02-M07.
visualization: Floor-plan heat-map of distance to nearest window (m) with the reach contour for k = 1 and k = 2
Lower, mid and upper typical plates side by side
Section sketch showing a daylight reach cone
Stacked bar of percent area within reach by programme
outputs: Rooms flagged below proxy thresholds (feed P02-M07, programme, structure and core-position modules)
modules.human_judgment: Where to put cores, services and non-daylit programme; acceptable depth for offices versus residential bedrooms; use of light wells, atria or double-height public floors; occupant wellbeing beyond the metric.
modules.limits: Geometric proxy only. Ignores glazing, neighbours (unless an obstruction angle is supplied), blinds and climate. The reach multiplier and limiting-depth formula are recalled, not opened. Daylight factor assumes an overcast sky and is not climate-based. Vancouver Building By-law window rules were not checked.

modules.name: Interior daylight (sDA, ASE, EN 17037)
modules.design_question: Do representative floors reach sDA, ASE and EN 17037 daylight targets once neighbours, glazing, operable shades and plate depth are included?
modules.effort: L: about 10-14 dev-days (server-side Radiance pipeline with aperture groups and shade states)
inputs: Representative floors (lower, mid, upper): plate, facade WWR, glazing VT, head height (Advanced presets)
Interior reflectances and shading devices with shade transmittance (default 0.05)
Context massing and NorthFrame from P02-M01
EPW file (CWEC 2020 or TMYx) and occupancy schedule (default 8:00-18:00)

parameters.name: Glazing visual transmittance
parameters.relationship: Higher VT raises sDA but also ASE and glare risk; VT below 0.4 can halve incoming light, above about 0.6 can cause glare.

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio
parameters.relationship: More glazing raises daylight at depth but increases ASE on the SW and NW facades of a street-aligned tower, and solar gain.

parameters.name: Plate depth
parameters.relationship: Deeper plate lowers sDA because points far from windows seldom reach 300 lux; the share of area at 300 lux for 50% of hours falls with distance (geometry plus simulation).

parameters.name: Neighbour obstruction by floor height
parameters.relationship: Lower floors see more obstruction from neighbouring towers; sDA rises with floor height above the context, so lower floors suit public or less daylight-dependent programme.

parameters.name: Occupied hours and sensor plane
parameters.relationship: Annual metrics depend on the schedule (default 8:00-18:00) and the plane: 0.762 m for LM-83, LEED and WELL IES routes; 0.85 m for EN 17037 (recalled, standard not opened). A longer schedule adds low-light hours and lowers sDA.

parameters.name: Shading devices and blinds
parameters.relationship: LEED v4.1 sDA is computed with an operable-shade schedule that keeps at most 2% of sensors at 1,000 lx or more direct sun (default shade transmittance 0.05); ASE is computed without blinds. Ignoring shades overstates sDA.

metrics.name: sDA 300 lx / 50% of hours with operable shades (LEED v4.1 Option 1)
metrics.good: At least 75% (3 credits), 55% (2), 40% (1), with a shade schedule keeping at most 2% of sensors at 1,000 lx direct; an extra credit or 'Exemplary performance' if every space reaches 55%
metrics.bad: Below 40%, or no shade schedule can comply: 0 credits
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] v1 computed sDA without shades. leed.py (opened) uses a shade schedule with the 2% rule and awards 0 credits if it cannot comply. USGBC and IES LM-83-12 texts not opened.
metrics.method: Run leed_option_one as published; report sDA with shades, blinds-up and blinds-down variants, and the per-space 55% check.

metrics.name: Annual sunlight exposure ASE 1000 lx / 250 h (no blinds)
metrics.good: 10% or less
metrics.bad: More than 10%: written glare-control note needed
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Open-source LEED v4.1 code (sensor fails ASE at 250 or more occupied hours above 1,000 lx direct; above 10% of area adds a note); IES LM-83 and LEED texts not opened.
metrics.method: Sensors receiving direct illuminance of at least 1,000 lx for 250 h or more, as a share of area.

metrics.name: EN 17037 target and minimum illuminance
metrics.unit: lx over % area for 50% of daylight hours
metrics.good: Target 300 / 500 / 750 lx (minimum / medium / high) over at least 50% of area; minimum 100 / 300 / 500 lx over 95%
metrics.bad: Fails the minimum tier at any level
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Open-source en17037.py (opened; 4,380 daylight hours = the half-year with most daylight); CEN standard not opened; sunlight-exposure and view criteria not modelled; reference plane 0.85 m recalled.

metrics.name: WELL v2 L06 daylight optimisation (IES route)
metrics.good: sDA 300/50% at least 55% (tier 1) or at least 75% (tier 2)
metrics.bad: Below 55%
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Values hard-coded in well.py (label WELL v2 Q2 2025, opened); WELL text not opened. EN 17037 route also exists in the code.

metrics.name: WELL v2 L01 light exposure and education (IES route, daylight part)
metrics.good: sDA 150 lx / 50% of hours over at least 30% of area
metrics.bad: Below 30%
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Values in well.py (opened); omitted in v1; WELL text not opened.

modules.method: 1) Build a Radiance model per representative floor: plate, facade, glazing VT, reflectances, aperture groups with operable shades (transmittance 0.05), context massing rotated by the NorthFrame. 2) Create an annual sky matrix from the EPW (Reinhart subdivision). 3) Place sensors at 0.762 m (LM-83, LEED, WELL IES route) and 0.85 m (EN 17037). 4) Run the matrix-based annual daylight recipe for hourly illuminance. 5) Post-process with leed_option_one and the WELL post-processors as published: sDA 300 lx/50% with the 2% direct-sun shade schedule, blinds-up and blinds-down variants, ASE 1000 lx/250 h, EN 17037 tiers (4,380 daylight hours), WELL L01 and L06. 6) Summarise per floor, programme and orientation, area-weighted. Run server-side; cache per floor.
visualization: Floor-plan false-colour map of daylight autonomy (0-100%) with the 50% contour
ASE map (hours above 1000 lx, 0-1000 h legend, 250 h contour)
Badges for LEED credit tier, EN 17037 tier and WELL tier linked to the threshold source and its status
Shade-feasibility panel: hours the 2% rule forces shades down, per floor
Floor-by-floor bar chart of sDA and ASE; facade overlay where direct sun exceeds the ASE limit
outputs: DaylightGrid {DA_pct, sDA_with_shades, sDA_blinds_up, ASE, EN17037_tier, WELL_L01, WELL_L06} per floor
Per-floor summary JSON (feeds programme net-lettable quality, lighting energy, facade and interior modules, and boards)
modules.human_judgment: Choice of representative floors and glazing strategy; accepting deep plates for public or cultural programme; balance of glare, views and privacy; whether residential-unit rules apply; qualitative spatial quality that the metrics do not capture.
modules.limits: Representative floors only. Typical-year weather. Partitions and furniture unknown at schematic design. LEED and WELL are rating systems, not Vancouver code; Vancouver Building By-law natural-light rules were not checked. Thresholds come from open-source code, not the primary standards. Heavy compute needs a server. ASE excludes blinds by design.

modules.name: Sky view, neighbour-facade exposure and reflected-sun screen
modules.design_question: How much open sky and direct sun do street-level points and neighbouring tower facades keep, and does the proposal's glazing reflect sun onto streets or neighbours?
modules.effort: M: about 5-7 dev-days for SVF and neighbour sun hours; reflected-sun screen is a roadmap sub-mode (about 3-4 more dev-days)
inputs: Proposed massing and context massing on the terrain mesh
Sample points: ground grid in public realm (1.5 m); facade grid or window centres on neighbouring towers facing the site
NorthFrame and SunVectorSet from P02-M01
Optional (roadmap): glazing specular reflectance and facade curvature (Advanced mode)

parameters.name: Tower height and podium setback
parameters.relationship: Street-level SVF falls as height-to-width of the street canyon rises; setting the tower back from the frontage above the podium raises sidewalk SVF (geometry).

parameters.name: Street, lane and mid-block link width
parameters.relationship: Narrow lanes and mid-block connections between tall faces have low SVF; widening or stepping the walls raises it (geometry).

parameters.name: Sample height and plane
parameters.relationship: Point-at-height evaluates sky exposure; a plane or oriented surface gives true sky view (fraction of sky seen from a surface), as defined in Ladybug Sky Mask. Ground SVF at 1.5 m is a team preset.

parameters.name: Patch density
parameters.relationship: Higher sky-patch subdivision raises accuracy and compute time; low density mis-estimates SVF near narrow gaps.

parameters.name: Tree canopy
parameters.relationship: Canopy lowers real SVF below the massing-only value; not modelled here, which overestimates SVF where trees exist (limit).

parameters.name: Neighbour facade position and proposal height
parameters.relationship: On 22 Sept shadows sweep NW through N to NE (306-52 degrees) up to about 590 m for 300 m of height, so neighbour facades facing the proposal on that side lose most direct sun; wider plates widen the lost band (geometry).

parameters.name: Glazing reflectance and facade curvature (roadmap)
parameters.relationship: Higher specular reflectance and concave curvature raise reflected-beam intensity and can focus it; a concave glass tower at 20 Fenchurch Street focused sun onto streets in 2013 (precedent, not a threshold).

metrics.name: Street-level sky view factor (cosine-weighted)
metrics.good: Context markers only, no pass/fail: Local Climate Zone compact high-rise band (recalled about 0.2-0.4)
metrics.bad: Not used as a pass/fail: a 244-305 m CBD tower would mark almost every street bad
metrics.basis: LCZ values are classification descriptors, not performance targets (r1). Stewart and Oke 2012 not opened; WUDAPT pages show no numbers.

metrics.name: Change in SVF vs baseline context at mid-block links and transit plaza
metrics.good: No decrease
metrics.bad: Decrease of 0.1 or more
metrics.basis: Editable preset for design comparison; no sourced threshold. The only judged SVF metric.

metrics.name: Change in direct sun hours on neighbouring-tower facade points vs baseline (22 Sept, 21 Dec)
metrics.good: No loss at residential or hotel windows
metrics.bad: More than 20% loss of a point's sun hours on either date
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no sourced Vancouver or Canadian threshold for neighbour facades (a similar UK relative-loss test was not opened).
metrics.method: DirectSunStudy-type intersection on facade points, proposal minus baseline.

metrics.name: Reflected-sun screen (roadmap)
metrics.good: No ground or facade receiver lies inside a specular beam from proposal glazing on any study date
metrics.bad: Any receiver hit, or concave or focusing glazing present
metrics.basis: Geometric screen only; no Vancouver or BC threshold for reflected irradiance or luminance was found.

modules.method: 1) Generate sample points: ground grid at 1.5 m on the public realm and a facade grid (window centres) on neighbouring towers. 2) Build a sky dome (Tregenza or Reinhart patches) at each point. 3) Cast rays through proposal plus context on terrain; SVF is the cosine-weighted fraction of unobstructed patch solid angle (name the weighting in the output). 4) Compute direct sun hours on neighbour-facade points for 22 Sept and 21 Dec with DirectSunStudy logic. 5) Output SVF and sun hours per point plus deltas against baseline. 6) Roadmap reflected-sun screen: mirror each sun vector in every glazed face and flag receivers inside the beam (screen only, no glare level). 7) Draw fisheye sky masks with sun-path overlay; use LB Sky Mask as reference and UMEP SVF as raster cross-check.
visualization: False-colour SVF map on public ground (0-1 legend with Local Climate Zone band markers, labelled 'context only')
Fisheye (stereographic or equidistant) sky-mask diagrams at 3-5 chosen points with sun-path overlay
Delta SVF map vs baseline; histogram of SVF by public space
Elevation of each neighbouring tower coloured by sun-hour loss (blue = none, red = loss) for 22 Sept and 21 Dec
Roadmap: plan and elevation with reflected-beam rays from glazed faces to hit receivers
outputs: DeltaSVF (feeds wind/thermal comfort, public-realm and human-scale, daylight and board modules)
modules.human_judgment: What degree of enclosure is desirable: intimate street vs open sky and mountain views; 'City in Nature' and cultural sightlines; whether low SVF in lanes is acceptable for character; how much neighbour sun loss is acceptable and for whom; glazing choice versus reflection risk.
modules.limits: Geometric only: no trees, canopies or weather. The link between SVF and heat-island intensity or pedestrian comfort is climatological and not calibrated for Vancouver. LCZ bands are context markers, not targets. The reflected-sun screen has no glare threshold and ignores curvature focusing unless modelled. Accuracy depends on sky-patch density.

sources.extract: Summer 2013: curved glass acted as a concave mirror and focused direct sun, up to two hours a day, onto streets to the south; parked cars were damaged. Temporary screening approved September 2013; permanent awning installed 2014. Precedent for a reflected-sun screen, not a threshold.

flags.detail: Candidate sources (ASHRAE 90.1 primary and secondary sidelit zones at 1 and 2 times head height; BRE / BS 8206-2 limiting depth) are recalled, not opened. Proxy borrows LEED sDA tiers. Replace by P02-M07 results where available.

flags.detail: BRE document not opened. UK housing amenity criterion, not a Vancouver requirement; r1 computes it over the whole day on 21 March and labels it a UK comparison.

flags.claim: LEED v4.1, WELL v2 and EN 17037 daylight thresholds
flags.detail: Evidence is the open-source honeybee-radiance-postprocess code (re-read in r1) and Wikipedia; USGBC, IES LM-83-12, WELL and CEN texts were not opened. flags.correction: Parks, schools and the s.4.2 plazas (Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square, Dilawri Square South): no new shadow within property lines, exceptions possible. Other urban plazas and miniparks: minimise where possible, report m2 and coverage %, no pass/fail.

flags.correction: Davie Village 10:00-16:00, Robson Village 10:00-15:00; north sidewalk only, curb to building face.

flags.correction: Rule 4.3.1: no shadow on the cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 PST on 11 Nov, in addition to the s.3.1 rules; exceptions only with comprehensive public and stakeholder engagement (4.3.2).

flags.detail: Guideline ss.4.1.1, 4.2.1 per reviewer; v1 relied on draft coverage (S06).

flags.detail: Guideline ss.5.1, 5.1.1 per reviewer. With L/H about 1.9-2.0 at 10:00 and 16:00, a 20 m level difference moves a shadow edge about 40 m.

flags.correction: Exception grounds are social housing, below-market rental, a public childcare facility, heritage conservation or a major city-building priority (3.1.2), and need a shadow rationale statement and a 15-minute Detailed study (5.2); staff weigh topography, duration and vulnerable users (3.1.3).

flags.detail: Re-read in r1 from leed.py in honeybee-radiance-postprocess (S21). WELL L01 (sDA 150 lx/50% over 30%) was also omitted.

unresolved_relationships: Tower floor-plate width, shape and orientation relative to the 45-degree grid versus hours of shadow on specific Table-1 points and versus sDA/ASE: only geometry is derived; the City links larger floor plates to solar-access compliance but the figures were not opened. A solar-envelope sweep by tower position on the 79.2 x 144.8 m block is not yet specified.

How the Downtown Peninsula guidelines measure 'new shadow' (area tolerance, sensor grid, small gaps, treatment of terrain at the receiver): no tolerance was reported by the reviewer and the author could not open the PDF.
Time step and format required for the 11 Nov cenotaph check (4.3.1): 15 minutes is assumed; the Detailed-study rule was reported only for 22 Sept.

Definition and source of 'known proposed developments' (s.5.1) and of City or open 3D context models for existing and approved towers: the open-data catalogue lists DEM, LiDAR, footprints and contours but no 3D massing dataset; height attributes of footprints were not verified.
Mapping between Table-1 classes and the Park Board classification field in City open data, and a complete polygon source for plazas that are not Park Board parks.
Quantitative link between sun hours and the usability or comfort of Vancouver public spaces: the City describes benefits qualitatively; no numeric relationship found.
Daylight reach as a multiple of window head height: ASHRAE 90.1 sidelit zones and the BRE/BS 8206-2 limiting-depth rule are candidates, but no source was opened.
Irradiation thresholds for facade and roof PV viability in Vancouver: none sourced (Compagnon 2004 not opened).

Vancouver and BC overheating compliance path and thresholds for tall residential and hotel towers: Passive House overheating frequency (Building Criteria v10c) and the City Energy Modelling Guidelines comfort limit not opened.
Relationship between solar gain on glazing and TEDI for this tower: needs a thermal model outside this packet; only the HBP s.2.2 target (reviewer-read) is known.
SVF versus pedestrian comfort and heat-island intensity in Vancouver: Oke and LCZ literature not opened; no Vancouver-specific relationship found.
Whether Vancouver Building By-law natural-light or window-area rules apply to tall-tower floors and how they relate to sDA: not checked.

Acceptable reflected irradiance or luminance from glazed facades onto streets and neighbours (Vancouver or BC): no threshold found; the reflected-sun screen is geometric only and ignores curvature focusing unless modelled.

notes: Method and caveats (r1, 21 Oct 2026). The WebSearch budget was already used up, so research used direct fetches only. vancouver.ca and guidelines.vancouver.ca are behind a Cloudflare block: WebFetch got HTTP 403 and curl got a block page; this was not circumvented and no PDF was saved.
